subject.title: Azure OpenAI Responses throws 400 when prompt_cache_key is sent to endpoints that do not support it

question: Should Azure OpenAI Responses keep sending `prompt_cache_key` by default for native Azure routes, or should Azure require explicit opt-in for prompt-cache hints?
rationale: Current code, docs, and tests intentionally keep prompt-cache hints on native Azure, but the report says at least one Azure endpoint rejects the field and does not provide enough live detail to distinguish unsupported deployment drift from a default-policy bug.

options.title: Keep default and document opt-out
options.body: Keep native Azure prompt-cache hints by default, require affected deployments to set `cacheRetention: "none"` or a compat opt-out, and add focused docs/tests for the Azure opt-out path.

options.title: Make Azure prompt-cache opt-in
options.body: Stop sending Azure `prompt_cache_key` unless the model explicitly opts in, reducing 400 risk but potentially losing cache affinity for supported Azure deployments.

options.title: Request live Azure proof first
options.body: Ask for the exact deployment, model, API version, and redacted 400 body before choosing a code or docs change.

recommendation.title: Keep default and document opt-out
recommendation.body: Keep native Azure prompt-cache hints by default, require affected deployments to set `cacheRetention: "none"` or a compat opt-out, and add focused docs/tests for the Azure opt-out path.
